events.title: The Bolshevik Revolution and the war on religion
events.shortBlurb: The seizure of Petrograd opened one of the longest and bloodiest persecutions the Christian East had ever endured…
body: On 7 November 1917 — 25 October by the Old-Style calendar Russia then kept — Lenin's Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government and stormed the Winter Palace in Petrograd. Within weeks the new regime turned against religion, decreeing in January 1918 the separation of Church and State and the seizure of ecclesiastical property, and setting in motion decades of official atheism.

The Russian Orthodox Church, which had only that same year restored the Moscow patriarchate under Patriarch Tikhon, saw its monasteries closed, its clergy imprisoned or shot, and its faithful driven underground; Tikhon publicly anathematized the persecutors. The Catholics of the former empire, both Latin and Eastern-rite, shared in the suffering, their bishops and priests among the martyrs and prisoners of the coming years.

The Holy See watched with alarm as the persecution spread with Soviet power. Pope Pius XI, who had served as nuncio in the region, condemned atheistic communism in the 1937 encyclical Divini Redemptoris, warning that it sought "to destroy the social order and to undermine the very foundations of Christian civilization."

sources.text: Pope Pius XI, encyclical Divini Redemptoris (19 March 1937), vatican.va
